subject: Recap & next steps: perf targets, context sizing, and test plan for Cobalt Systems
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@cobaltsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap & next steps: perf targets, context sizing, and test plan for Cobalt Systems

Jordan — thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the technical deep-dive:

Summary of asks / constraints from Cobalt (as I captured them):
- Target p95 end-to-end latency for typical chat flows: <= 250 ms for short prompts (<1k tokens).
- Long-context recall requests (searching >10k tokens of user history) can tolerate up to 1.2s p95 but should stream partial responses.
- Peak concurrency expected by launch: ~75 concurrent active users generating requests (~30 rps sustained, 120 rps burst).
- Average per-request token mix: ~1k input / 800 output; occasional heavy transcripts up to 12k input + 3k output.
- SLOs important for business-critical flows (billing / checkout): 99.9% availability and a <350 ms p95 for the “checkout” route.

Key open questions for the tech deep-dive:
1) For the heavy transcripts (15k total tokens), do you need the full 12k input to be kept in the main prompt each time, or can we rely on KV cache + indexed retrieval for older history?
2) Is streaming required for all long responses, or only for the recall flows?
3) Are there any hard constraints on the number of concurrent long-context requests?

Proposed plan / next steps:
- Technical deep-dive with our runtime team (Vivek on CC) to scope quantization and batching impact — propose Wed 4/7 10:00 PT.
- Initial perf baseline: Redwood will run a targeted load test modeling 30 rps with the mixed token distribution above and provide p50/p95/p99 numbers and per-token cost estimates.
- Deliverables: perf matrix (attached), recommended config (model size, quantization, batch sizing), and a mutual action plan for pilot.

Attachments: redwood_perf_profile.pdf (profile of candidate models + estimates), context_capacity_proposal.xlsx (initial capacity config), mutual_action_plan.docx (high level milestones).

If that aligns, Jordan — can you loop in procurement for paperwork and Lena for security/compliance so we can make sure the SOC2/Security checklist is available before the pilot?

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
https://redwood.com

From: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@cobaltsys.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@cobaltsys.com>, procurement@cobaltsys.com
Date: 2026-04-05T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: perf targets, context sizing, and test plan for Cobalt Systems

Thanks Aisha — this looks right and appreciated the clarity. A couple quick clarifications:

- For the heavy transcripts: we prefer to keep the most recent 6k tokens in the prompt and have the rest accessible via retrieval if that simplifies latency, but we need full-document grounding when a legal-regression search is requested (ad-hoc, maybe 1% of calls).
- Streaming: yes, streaming is required for any response where the output >500 tokens (so broadly for recall-heavy responses).
- Concurrent long-context requests: estimate ~8–12 concurrent heavy sessions during peak (not huge, but their p95 matters).

Procurement on CC — can you confirm timing for NDA + standard MSA? Lena — happy to share an SR with our security team if you send over the inbound questionnaire.

—Jordan

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@cobaltsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-06T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: perf targets, context sizing, and test plan for Cobalt Systems

Jordan — perfect, thanks for the clarifications. A few technical notes to set expectations before Wed: 

- Context strategy: the approach you described (6k prompt + retrieval for older history) is the most cost/latency efficient. For the 1% legal-regression searches where the full doc is required, we recommend pinning a quantized, smaller-architecture model variant that prioritizes throughput for batch jobs; Redwood can route those queries to a dedicated pool to avoid affecting low-latency chat flows.

- Latency vs tokens: empirically, for our 13B quantized variants we see ~40–70 ms per generated token on GPU at steady-state (depending on batch size and model). That means a 800-token output will add ~32–56 ms on top of dispatch/IO overhead; the bigger contributor for long-context requests is attention cost on the encoder side when the input is 6k–12k tokens. For those, end-to-end p95 can grow into the 700–1,200 ms range if not batched or if KV cache misses are frequent.

- Streaming helps perceived latency: partial tokens can be forwarded as they’re generated so your UI sees the start of the answer much earlier (p50 for first byte can be <120 ms for typical prompts).

- Concurrency and batching: with your projected 30 rps and bursts to 120 rps, batching increases throughput but can add 10–80 ms depending on target latency SLO. We’ll propose a batch window policy in the perf matrix that trades a small p50 increase for big cost savings at p95 targets.

Proposed deliverables for the Wed deep-dive:
- Live perf baseline (30 rps mixed traffic) with and without streaming enabled.
- Configs: model variant choices, quantization level, batch window, and KV cache settings.
- Pilot plan: sample dataset, success criteria (p95 targets, error budget), and rollback/fallback policy.

I’ve attached the perf profile and a starter capacity sheet. If procurement/Legal needs SOC2, Lena — we can share our SOC2 report and a short runbook for audit items; Vivek can own the compliance artifacts for the pilot.

Thoughts? If Wed 4/7 10:00 PT still works I’ll send a calendar invite with a short agenda and list of people we’ll bring from the runtime team.

Best,
Aisha

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@cobaltsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-06T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: perf targets, context sizing, and test plan for Cobalt Systems

Adding a brief operational note from the runtime side:

- Dedicated pool recommendation: for predictability on the checkout route we suggest reserving a small dedicated pool (2–4 GPUs depending on model choice) to isolate the critical path. That avoids noisy-neighbor latency from bursty analysis jobs.
- KV cache tuning: enable TTL-based caching of frequently referenced context slices (we can map to your retrieval keys). Cache hit rates >85% materially reduce end-to-end p95 for long-context flows.
- Suggested pilot config (conservative): 1 x 70B quantized model for high-quality recall jobs routed to a batch pool, and 2 x 13B quantized instances in the low-latency pool with streaming enabled.

I’ll bring benchmark snapshots to Wed’s meeting. Also, Marissa — we should capture pricing scenarios for both dedicated-reserved and burstable on-demand plans so procurement has clear options.

-Vivek

From: procurement@cobaltsys.com <procurement@cobaltsys.com>

Cc: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@cobaltsys.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@cobaltsys.com>

Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: perf targets, context sizing, and test plan for Cobalt Systems

Thanks — procurement here. We’re aligned to move forward with an initial 8-week pilot pending NDA and SOC2 review. Action items we need from Redwood: 
1) NDA (we can send our standard, but if Redwood has a mutual NDA we can use that)
2) SOC2 Type II report and a contact for any technical audit questions (email + low-level artifact list).
3) DocuSign-ready MSA or statement of work template for a pilot (we prefer a short SOW).

Please send the above links to procurement@cobaltsys.com and cc Jordan and Lena. We’ll target execution within 7 business days.

Regards,
Cobalt Procurement
